searchText: Just some red text at the top (or maybe black text in a red box, I'm not a UI designer) that says something like "This is just a Draft, it is not ready for general use or implementation as it is likely to change." Similar for all other statuses besides final. Once the banner is up, changing the text is easy so I recommend getting something up and then soliciting feedback. Don't worry too much about the exact wording for now. Whatever you think sounds good. Can someone familiar with Ruby, or with free time to go through the README process, validate this: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3598 are you open to upgrading the min ruby version 2.1.x to 2.6.x? all versions <2.6 are already EOL. having some issues installing 2.1 to validate the master branch also it also looks like the PR is trying to add dependencies for ruby 3.0 e.g. webrick for jekyll. if you're ok, i can validate the PR and upgrade the READme specify it Hmm, I have no opinion, but I also have no way of validating anything or asserting whether any of this is a good or bad idea. 😬 alright, let me validate on 3.0 and update the PR with notes. happy to get a second rubyist to echo this. but i've had no issues maintaining my blog on ruby 3 jekyll :) Hey 👋 Is there any EIP open for mitigating MEV? I would like to contribute to help reduce the impact of it <@!712770661432426666> i'm not aware of any open eips - i recommend hopping in the flashbots discord if you aren't already and asking them what the latest mitigation techniques are I am already in the flashbot discord, but most of their recommendations are for mitigating MEV using flashbots. While my idea would be if we could use the "envelope pattern" so transactions would be only visible once they have been executed trying to help get eip_validator to 100% passing. these older eips are invalid (missing status) - any recommendations on what status to assign them? What is the short version of how you would make it so miners could produce valid blocks without being able to execute the transactions in them? <@!778533694863966228> which eip_validator are you running? This sounds like the encrypt/decrypt (or commit/reveal) pattern. Have you seen https://shutter.ghost.io/ ? using master branch, just running the eip_validator 0.8.2 as per the installation instructions install instructions probably out of date, `eipv` used now to statically check the frontmatter https://github.com/lightclient/eipv I think the flashbots guys also have partially explored/discussed this (e.g. see Timelock encryption and threshold encryption sections) https://ethresear.ch/t/mev-sgx-a-sealed-bid-mev-auction-design/9677 oh i see. are all validations moved to eipv? any additional setup steps to take note? this is a good place to see what is run in CI: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/.travis.yml currently there is two merge bots, one is an older python impl and one is a newer github ci impl they do some validation too but mainly try to facilitate notifying ppl when their actions are required and auto merging things when the correct ppl have approved ah ok. so in this PR https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3599, the first `Auto-Merge Bot` is the older python bot. are we keeping it? because it looks like the travis-ci bot is also doing htmlproofer and eip-validator (on eipv) that's the new bot, i'm not sure what the issue is started from here: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/746566142700814426/849992298854744134 i thought the Ask was to see if the PR#3598 is necessary. it seems to add a few new dependencies. i'm validating that the current installation on ruby 2 is still working fine, but want to recommend a bump to min version ruby 2.7 in the README. gotcha - bumping to 2.7 seems fine, i'm just noting that i don't understand what is causing the new bot to fail IMOH something like - Miners choose tx's to include in the block - Then, the order is stablish - The tx gets reveal and gets executed - If we can add more tx to reach the gas block, repeat from 1st step - If gas reach the limit, the tx remaining will return to mempool What happens if the transaction is not revealed? What happens if it is not revealed in time? https://twitter.com/josephdelong/status/1400506331145121795?s=20 > improving Ethereum > Documenting a standard
